s: A solutions architect is designing an AWS account structure for a company that consists of multiple teams. All the teams will work in the same AWS Region. The company needs a VPC that is connected to the on-premises network. The company expects less than 50 Mbps of total traffic to and from the on-premises network. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively? (Select TWO.)
o: Create an AWS Cloud Formation template that provisions a VPC and the required subnets. Deploy the template to each AWS account.
Create an AWS Cloud Formation template that provisions a VPC and the required subnets. Deploy the template to a shared services account Share the subnets by using AWS Resource Access Manager.
Use AWS Transit Gateway along with an AWS Site-to-Site VPN for connectivity to the on-premises network. Share the transit gateway by using AWS Resource Access Manager.
Use AWS Site-to-Site VPN for connectivity to the on-premises network.
Use AWS Direct Connect for connectivity to the on-premises network.

w.y: One shared VPC in a shared services account, with its subnets shared to the team accounts through AWS RAM, avoids duplicating VPCs and on-premises connections. Under 50 Mbps is easily handled by a Site-to-Site VPN, which is far cheaper than Direct Connect. With a single VPC there is no need for a transit gateway.

o.A: A VPC in every account needs separate on-premises connectivity for each one, which raises cost and complexity.
o.B: Correct: VPC sharing through RAM gives every team one centrally connected VPC at no extra charge.
o.C: A transit gateway adds attachment and data-processing charges that aren't needed when there is only one shared VPC.
o.D: Correct: Site-to-Site VPN is the low-cost choice for under 50 Mbps of hybrid traffic.
o.E: Direct Connect has port-hour and circuit costs that aren't justified for under 50 Mbps.

s: Share your VPC subnets with other accounts
